title: Prove the arithmetic series sum formula by writing the series forwards and backwards and adding
content: To prove Sn = (n/2)[2a+(n-1)d], write out Sn as the sum of terms from a up to the last term a+(n-1)d, then write the same sum again with the terms in reverse order (from a+(n-1)d down to a). Adding the two versions term-by-term, every pair sums to the same value 2a+(n-1)d, and there are n such pairs, giving 2Sn = n[2a+(n-1)d]. Dividing by 2 gives the required formula. This 'reverse and add' idea is the standard way to derive (or re-derive from scratch in an exam) any arithmetic series sum formula.
